UnaMentisTests
Pinned expected verdicts for the golden parity matrix
(MODULE_SDK_SPEC.md Phase 4). Generated by running the CURRENT
KBAnswerValidator over KBGoldenParityMatrix, then frozen. These values are
the migration contract: they must hold before AND after the KB validation
lift into the host ResponseEvaluationService.
Each entry maps a case id to (expectedCorrect, expectedMatchType.rawValue).
Two entries encode real current-code quirks worth preserving as contract:
- `strict-typo-rejected` / `strict-phonetic-rejected` are CORRECT at
`.strict` because `.strict` gates only the ENHANCED tiers (synonym,
phonetic, n-gram, token, linguistic). Baseline Levenshtein still runs, and
both inputs fall within its distance threshold. Only `strictMode` (a
separate Config flag) disables Levenshtein.
- `nearmiss-diff-number` ("100" vs "1000") is CORRECT because Levenshtein
distance is 1, inside the fuzzy threshold. The numeric evaluator inherits
the same fuzzy pass the text path uses.

UnaMentisTests
The golden parity matrix for Knowledge Bowl answer validation
(MODULE_SDK_SPEC.md section 13, Phase 4).
This matrix is the migration contract for lifting KB's algorithmic answer
validation into the host `ResponseEvaluationService`. Each case captures a
distinct real-world input shape: exact matches, case and punctuation
variants, misspellings at varying edit distances, phonetic matches, synonym
hits, acceptable-answer hits, near misses that must stay wrong, empty and
garbage input, numeric answers, and multi-word answers with token
reordering.
Expected verdicts (`expectedCorrect`, `expectedMatch`) were generated by
running the CURRENT `KBAnswerValidator` over this matrix, not written by
hand. The same matrix runs against the new host service after the lift; both
must agree with these pinned values. See KBValidationGoldenParityTests.

UnaMentisTests
Golden parity suite for the Knowledge Bowl answer-validation migration
(MODULE_SDK_SPEC.md section 13, Phase 4). This is the migration contract.
It runs the full KBGoldenParityMatrix through the host evaluation service
and asserts each verdict matches the pinned KBGoldenParityExpected table.
The pinned table was generated by running the legacy `KBAnswerValidator`
(the code that was lifted) over this exact matrix BEFORE the lift, so a green
run here proves the host `DefaultResponseEvaluationService` reproduces the
old KB behavior case for case. This is the Phase 4 exit criterion
(MODULE_SDK_SPEC.md section 13).
